rules.statement: Apply a cross-cutting endpoint filter or convention for a family of endpoints once, on that family's shared `RouteGroupBuilder` (via `MapGroup`), rather than attaching it to each endpoint individually or installing process-wide middleware.
rules.why: Attaching it to each endpoint repeats the same wiring and is easy to forget on a new endpoint. Global middleware would also wrap endpoints outside the family.
rules.check: Look for the same `AddEndpointFilter`/convention call repeated on individual endpoints of one family, or for new app-wide middleware that only one endpoint family needs.

rules.statement: Register endpoints that are mapped by a family's route group only under that group's registration, so each endpoint is mapped exactly once and none is also mapped through the flat root-level endpoint collection.
rules.why: If an endpoint is registered in both places it gets mapped twice, and the copy mapped outside the group misses the group's filters and conventions.
rules.check: Check that a new endpoint in a grouped family is not also added to the root/flat endpoint provider registrations.

rules.statement: Make sure exceptions thrown by OAuth/OpenID endpoints are caught and returned as a standard OAuth error response (an `error` JSON body with the error's own status code), with a `500 server_error` fallback for unknown exceptions. Never let them escape to the framework.
rules.why: Exceptions that nothing handles surface as framework 500s or the developer exception page instead of protocol-compliant error responses.
rules.check: Look for new OpenID/OAuth endpoints mapped outside the group that has the exception filter, or for an exception handler that is registered but never called.

rules.statement: When an exception handler can be set per endpoint, resolve it per request with this precedence: the endpoint's own metadata first, then the DI-registered default handler.
rules.why: This lets individual endpoints customize error rendering while every other endpoint keeps the shared default.
rules.check: Check that filter/handler resolution reads endpoint metadata before falling back to the DI service, and does not ignore the metadata or reverse the order.

rules.statement: Add new extensibility as an extra opt-in tier alongside the existing public registration API, not by replacing or breaking it, and record every new public type and member in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`.
rules.why: Replacing the existing surface causes needless churn and breaking changes for consumers that don't need the new capability. Tracking new APIs keeps the public surface under control.
rules.check: Look for public registration methods or interfaces that were removed or changed incompatibly, and for new public API that is missing from `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`.

rules.statement: Do not let a composition-root or core assembly reference types specific to one feature family. Let the family plug its own behavior in through an abstraction that the core defines.
rules.why: Layering: the core must not know about family-specific concerns, so those concerns don't leak into the composition root.
rules.check: Look for new `using` directives or project references from a core/composition-root project to a feature-family project.
